newsitem.title: BELGIUM: "Time to kill" released in traumatised Belgium.
newsitem.headline: "Time to kill" released in traumatised Belgium.

text.p: "Time to kill", a U.S. film about a father who killed the men who raped his daughter, has been released in Belgium after a two-month delay imposed because of the paedophile sex murder scandal which has rocked the country.
"The atmosphere is less emotional now in Belgium, we think there will be no problem with the release," Warner Bros. Belgium Sales Manager Anthony Callebaut told Reuters on Thursday.

Director Joel Schumacher's film had been scheduled for release in September, just two weeks after a series of gruesome discoveries in a paedophile kidnap, abuse and murder case which has so far claimed the lives of four girls.
"We had already had some trial runs of the film here, but because of the Dutroux case we called it off," Callebaut said.
Convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux is the main suspect in the paedophile murder case.
Dutroux, one of 13 people charged in connection with the case, was released in 1992 -- 10 years early -- from a 13-year sentence for multiple child rape.

Schumacher's film -- an adaptation of a best-selling book by U.S. author John Grisham -- is the story of a black man who shoots the two white men who brutally raped and nearly killed his 10-year old daughter.
Jan Temmerman, film critic for Belgian daily De Morgen, questioned the decision to first delay and then release the film.

"If one censors something, you only draw attention to it. And if you really want to respect people's feelings, you don't release it at all. People are still very upset about the Dutroux case," he said.
